subject: history
topic: Why the 20th-century 'Green Revolution' created permanent soil nutrient depletion
angle: While the Green Revolution successfully boosted grain yields in India, it is linked to long-term soil fertility deterioration, land degradation, and ecological imbalance.
title: The Cost of the Green Revolution

hooks.text: Can the soil keep producing forever?
You were told it fed millions. The evidence links it to soil degradation.
You consume a system that is exhausting the earth.
A cracked field under a heavy sun.

reveal.headline: The Green Revolution linked to permanent soil health degradation.
reveal.body: The push for higher grain yields in India is linked to the loss of soil flora and fauna. It is also linked to systematic damages to the soil, groundwater, and ecosystem.

explain.headline: Yields plateau while soil health declines.
explain.body: The Green Revolution is linked to yield plateauing and insecurity for farmers. It is also linked to a larger share of public spending on input subsidies as soil fertility deteriorates.

matters.headline: The cost of your food is hidden in the earth.
matters.body: That may be why the food you eat relies on an increasingly fragile system. The land is losing its ability to sustain itself without constant intervention.

example.headline: The grain in your pantry.
example.body: You see a full bowl of rice or wheat. You do not see the depleted ground or the chemical inputs required to keep it there.

question.headline: What happens when the soil can no longer give?

verdict: The sources provide evidence that Green Revolution Technologies are linked to significant environmental and soil degradation in India and other regions.
caveat: The sources do not provide a specific quantification of the systematic damages caused to the soil or groundwater.
caption:
The Green Revolution was designed to boost grain yields. 

Research links these technologies to soil fertility deterioration, ecological imbalance, and groundwater damage. The studies do not provide a specific quantification of these damages.

How do you feel about the cost of our food systems?
